question: Which EV charging programs are open now?
html:
Three EV charging opportunities are open as of Oct 8, 2026. The nearest deadline is the SRTA New Bedford DC fast-charger install, due tomorrow (CET opportunity radar).

Open EV charging opportunities

OpportunityOwnerTypeCloses
New Bedford DCFC installSRTATransit depot charging bidOct 9, 2026
Neighborhood EV chargingCity of CambridgeFederal-aid municipal bidNov 10, 2026
NEVI developers' installer callGlobal Montello / Applegreen (MassDOT NEVI)Installer partnershipOct 31, 2026

All three come from the opportunity radar, which was generated Sep 24, 2026 (CET opportunity radar). Confirm each one is still open before committing crews or estimating hours.

What each one involves

  • SRTA New Bedford. This is depot DC fast-charger installation. The radar suggests bidding it from our Taunton office (CET opportunity radar).
  • Cambridge. This is neighborhood charging funded with federal aid. The radar flags MassDOT prequalification and DBE requirements to check now (CET opportunity radar). We give no view here on how those rules apply.
  • MassDOT NEVI installer call. The developers named in the memo are looking for installers for highway fast-charging sites. The radar also suggests offering the same partnership to Applegreen for its 2026 Maine NEVI awards. That could make this a multi-state DCFC pipeline (CET opportunity radar).

What we don't know yet

  • Contract values. The context gives no estimated value for any of the three. Bid documents, or the developers' site counts and charger specs, would supply them.
  • Maine NEVI timing. Applegreen's Maine awards are listed as a lead, not a posted solicitation. There is no due date or scope yet.
  • Other states. CT, RI, NH and VT charging programs are not itemized. Some state procurement portals blocked automated access, so the radar may be missing listings (CET opportunity radar).

Why EV charging matters

The growth plan names EV depot charging as one of the Phase 3 service lines meant to turn one-off bids into recurring contracts (CET growth plan). The plan's month-36 target assumes about a 25% recurring service mix (est., labelled an assumption in the CET growth plan).

Winning the install work now puts us first in line for the maintenance and uptime contracts that follow, and recurring service is where the growth plan expects the valuation multiple to improve.

Next actions

  1. SRTA bid. Finalize and submit the New Bedford DCFC bid from Taunton by Oct 9, 2026, or record a no-bid decision today.
  2. NEVI installer call. Respond to the MassDOT NEVI developers' call before Oct 31, 2026. In the same response, open the Maine partnership conversation with Applegreen.
  3. Cambridge eligibility. Have estimating confirm MassDOT prequalification status and DBE requirements for the Cambridge bid this week. This leaves time before the Nov 10, 2026 deadline.
  4. Missed listings. Pull EV charging solicitations by hand from CT, RI and NH procurement portals. This closes the coverage gap in the radar.
